title: Extraction: emails to structured orders (output format)
description: Free text in, structured data out. Shows the answer format saving output tokens.
question: Extract every order from these emails: the customer name, the product (as named in our catalogue: Keyboard, Monitor 27", USB-C cable, Headset), the quantity and the delivery date as YYYY-MM-DD.

toon.none:
The data below is in TOON.

TOON (Token-Oriented Object Notation) — how to read it:
- Indentation shows nesting; "key: value" is a field.
- key[N]{f1,f2,...}: is followed by N rows of comma-separated values in field order.
- key[N]: a,b,c is a list of N values; "- " starts an item of a list of objects.

<data>
emails[4]{from,subject,body}:
  customer1@example.com,Order request #1,"Hi, please send 3 keyboards to our Kraków office. We need them by 4 November 2026. Thanks, Marta Nowak"
  customer2@example.com,Order request #2,"Hello — Jan Kowalski here. I'd like to order one 27-inch monitor (Monitor 27\"), delivery on 2026-11-06 if possible."
  customer3@example.com,Order request #3,"Order from Acme Sp. z o.o.: 25 × USB-C cable. Delivery: 3rd of November 2026. Invoice to the usual address."
  customer4@example.com,Order request #4,"Could you ship two headsets for Ola Wiśniewska? Delivery date: Nov 10, 2026. Thank you!"
</data>

Question: Extract every order from these emails: the customer name, the product (as named in our catalogue: Keyboard, Monitor 27", USB-C cable, Headset), the quantity and the delivery date as YYYY-MM-DD.

Answer in TOON only (no prose, no code fences): orders[N]{customer,product,quantity,delivery_date}: followed by one row per item.

akd.none:
The data below is in AK-DATA.

AK-DATA (Arkadia Data Format): <a:type,b:type> is a header; (v1,v2) is a record whose values follow the header order.
<[a:type,...]>[(...),(...)] is a list of records sharing that header; headers nest, e.g. items:<[sku:string,qty:number]>.
{key:value} is a record with names; <type> or <any> before a value overrides the header type.
Strings are quoted; numbers, true, false, null as in JSON; /*...*/, $attr, #tag are metadata, not data.
A record with fewer values than its header has only the first fields; //$size=N// before list items is their count.

<data>
<emails:<[from:string, subject:string, body:string]>>
([
  (
    "customer1@example.com",
    "Order request #1",
    "Hi, please send 3 keyboards to our Kraków office. We need them by 4 November 2026. Thanks, Marta Nowak"
  ),
  (
    "customer2@example.com",
    "Order request #2",
    "Hello — Jan Kowalski here. I'd like to order one 27-inch monitor (Monitor 27\"), delivery on 2026-11-06 if possible."
  ),
  (
    "customer3@example.com",
    "Order request #3",
    "Order from Acme Sp. z o.o.: 25 × USB-C cable. Delivery: 3rd of November 2026. Invoice to the usual address."
  ),
  (
    "customer4@example.com",
    "Order request #4",
    "Could you ship two headsets for Ola Wiśniewska? Delivery date: Nov 10, 2026. Thank you!"
  )
])
</data>
